messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: customer=kronos; severity=P1; issue=possible cross-tenant data exposure in Dedicated VPC. Link: https://redwood.prod/incidents/2263456789 :rotating_light:
oncall-sre: I'm on it. Acknowledge and stand up a triage. Paging eng-runtime and security.
oncall-sre: Quick ask — did Kronos give an example payload or ETA for when this first appeared?
beth-cs: Customer sent two examples at 09:12 UTC, obfuscated PII fields but matching tenant ids. They want a live scrub and timeline. I uploaded artifacts to the case.
alex_garcia: Copy. Starting initial hypothesis: routing/prefix leak or KV cache collision between dedicated pool instances. Will grab routing table + last 24h KV access logs.
maria_cheng: I'll shadow for runtime. If it's routing, we may need to isolate the pool and enable strict egress rules. Suggest a temporary hold on new connections to the affected pool.
eng-runtime-bot: Runbook triggered: Tenant Isolation Playbook v2.3 -> https://runbooks.redwood/tenant-isolation. Suggested steps: 1) snapshot routing table 2) dump KV cache prefixes 3) disable autoscale for pool 4) flag metric anomalies.
samir: Oncall helper — can you post the pool id and node list? I want to check node-level logs for prefix mismatches.
oncall-sre: Affected pool: dedicated-kronos-pool-41. Nodes: g4-12-a(10.1.72.11), g4-12-a(10.1.72.12), g4-12-b(10.1.74.21).
alex_garcia: Pulling routing table snapshot now. Running: ```curl -sS "https://infraapi.internal/pools/dedicated-kronos-pool-41/routing" | jq .```
eng-runtime-bot: Routing snapshot saved to /tmp/incidents/2263456789/routing.json (sha256: b4f1c2...).
maria_cheng: KV cache check started. Querying prefixes where last_access_customer != owner_customer. Running quick grep on keyspace: ```grep -R "owner: kronos" /var/kvcache/mappings | grep -v "tenant:kronos"```
eng-security: Stop-the-line question: do we have any evidence of outbound data transfer to third parties? Need egress logs.
beth-cs: Customer hasn't reported external exfiltration, only seeing other tenant identifiers in payloads returned from the API.
alex_garcia: Early result: found 3 request traces where response payload included an unexpected tenant prefix that belongs to customer-88. Traces correspond to nodes g4-12-a(10.1.72.11) at 09:05-09:09 UTC.
samir: That points to prefix routing table mismatch on node 11. I'm going to cordon that node and route new traffic off it. Executing drain now.
oncall-sre: Actioned: cordon node 10.1.72.11, set weight=0. Traffic should shift within 30s. Monitoring.
eng-runtime-bot: Autoscale and rebalancer paused for pool dedicated-kronos-pool-41.
maria_cheng: While draining, I captured KV key dump from node 11: suspicious keys show overlapping prefix hashes for tenant 88 and kronos. Dump attached in artifacts.
alex_garcia: Looks like a stale routing cache entry wasn't invalidated after a recent redeploy. Patch candidate: ensure cache invalidation on route table writes. I'll open a PR after triage.
eng-security: Forensics: collecting full request/response bodies for the 3 traces and all keys read by those requests. Tagging as evidence. Legal: @legal-erin FYI — potential customer data exposure.
legal-erin: Thanks — I'll stand by for redacted examples and timeline. We'll need to assess notification obligations; please preserve logs and avoid modifying evidence.
beth-cs: I told Kronos we're investigating and temporarily routed them to a fallback pool (dedicated-kronos-failover-1). They accepted the mitigation but want ETA for full scrub.
samir: Node 10.1.72.11 drained successfully and isolated. No new suspect traces after 09:16 UTC.
oncall-sre: Can we confirm whether any other customers had requests during the window that might have been served by node 11?
alex_garcia: Cross-checking request logs now. Running a windowed search for 09:00-09:20 UTC for node 10.1.72.11. Query: ```SELECT * FROM request_logs WHERE node='10.1.72.11' AND ts >= '2026-03-15T09:00:00Z' AND ts <= '2026-03-15T09:20:00Z'```
eng-runtime-bot: Preliminary: 14 distinct customer ids served. Flagging customers 88, 701, and 4093 as having potentially interleaved responses.
eng-security: Escalate scope: send notifications to CS for affected customers. We'll coordinate timeline and ask customers for sample payloads. Beth, can you handle comms for these?
beth-cs: On it. I'll open CS cases and request example payloads and whether they observed anomalies. Also asking for retention window needs.
alex_garcia: Mitigation next steps: 1) Full cache wipe on node 11 (done but node isolated) 2) Route table validation across controller plane 3) Deploy hotfix to force invalidation on writes 4) Reintroduce node after validation.
maria_cheng: I validated controller route table — write logs show a write at 08:58 that had an error but returned success to controller; invalidation hook didn't fire. I'll attach controller log snippet: ```2026-03-15T08:58:12Z WARN route_write: write_ack but invalidate_hook_failed: timeout=30s```
eng-security: Good evidence. Recommend rolling forward hotfix to prevent recurrence and run a full audit across all pools for similar failed invalidations.
legal-erin: Please document timeline: first observed 09:05 UTC, node isolated 09:16 UTC, evidence secured. We'll draft initial notification template.
beth-cs: CS case IDs created: CS-13421 (Kronos), CS-13422 (Customer-88), CS-13423 (Customer-701), CS-13424 (Customer-4093). Communicated mitigation and asked for samples.
samir: I'm running a cluster-wide check for nodes with invalidation_timeout > 10s. If matches, will list and block auto-rollouts until fix.
oncall-sre: Temporary mitigation approved: block autoscale and rebalancer globally for dedicated pools until hotfix verifies. Ops lead please confirm.
eng-runtime-bot: Emergency hotfix PR created: https://git.redwood/pr/9987 - title: "force-invalidate-route-cache-on-write". CI queued.
alex_garcia: If CI passes, schedule hotfix to staging first, then canary to 5% of pools, then full ramp. We'll coordinate with oncall windows.
eng-security: Collecting confirmation from forensic artifacts prior to any node rejoin. No reintroductions until evidence clean.
legal-erin: Also recommend preserving customer communication drafts in secure doc with limited access. I'll lead that.
beth-cs: Customer Kronos acknowledged temporary route to failover pool; remains online with some latency. They asked for a root-cause ETA — we told them 24-48h for full report, pending hotfix results.
samir: Cluster-wide scan returns 2 other nodes with occasional invalidate timeouts; I'll add them to the list and coordinate maintenance.
oncall-sre: Summary of immediate actions: isolate node 10.1.72.11, pause autoscale/rebalancer, secure evidence, create CS cases, create hotfix PR. Responsible: alex_garcia & samir. Target: restore normal traffic by 2026-03-16 12:00 UTC (tentative).
eng-security: Follow-ups: full audit of route invalidation logs, customer impact report, notification decision documented.
legal-erin: I'll review notification thresholds once we have confirmed affected record counts.
beth-cs: I'll keep customers updated and share any customer-provided samples directly to eng-security channel with redaction.
alex_garcia: Will update thread with PR/CI results and plan for canary.
oncall-sre: Thanks team. Keep this thread for technical updates. If you need an external postmortem channel, create a new thread after stabilizing.
eng-runtime-bot: Note: runbook step completed: evidence snapshot, isolation, mitigation. Next runbook recommended task: full-sweep-audit (queued).
eng-security: Noted. We will hold forensic images for 90 days.
legal-erin: Logging complete. I'll follow up with a compliance checklist.
final-note: oncall-sre marked thread as ongoing — next update expected within 2 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
